findings.title: New parsers verified against the real CLI's JSON shapes; failures are explicit
findings.description: Description: `purchase_verdicts.not_caught_up_report` consumes `coverage` documents whose session entries carry `session_date`/`status`/`unit_ids` as `tick_coverage.TickCoverage.to_dict()` renders them, and `purchase_accounting.accounting_rows` consumes `accounting_futures._product_payload` output (verified in `src/manta_trading/cli/commands/accounting_futures.py:59` and `src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py`). Missing keys raise `CutoverError` naming the key (e.g. `accounting_rows` at `scripts/purchase_accounting.py:57-95`), unknown session buckets stop the exit rule (`_unaccounted`, `scripts/purchase_verdicts.py:237-245`), and `verify_cme_sessions.py` genuinely accepts `--calendar <id> <dirs...>` with exits 0/1/2 as `run_session_check` maps them. Tests pin all of this through the real rendering functions rather than hand-built dicts.

findings.title: Unused constant EXIT_USAGE
findings.description: Description: `EXIT_USAGE = 2` (added beside `JOURNAL_LINES`) is never referenced — `main()` returns `int(exc.code or 0)` directly from the argparse `SystemExit`. Ruff will not flag an unused module constant, so it will linger as dead code. Delete it or use it in the `SystemExit` handler.

findings.title: Duplicated "want has no end date" guard
findings.description: Description: `coverage_reads()` and `purchase_verdicts.latest_want_end()` (`scripts/purchase_verdicts.py:73-87`) each iterate `TICK_UNIVERSE` and raise the same `CutoverError` ("…want has no end date") for an open-ended want — two copies of the same validation loop with the same message. A shared helper (e.g. in `cutover_304_checks`, which both modules already import or can import) would state the "every end is fixed" invariant once, per the project's one-value-one-source rule.

findings.title: Import order in cutover_304_evidence.py likely violates the required isort rule
findings.description: Description: The new `import purchase_accounting` / `import purchase_verdicts` lines are placed *before* `from cutover_304_checks import ...` / `from cutover_common import ...`, i.e. `p` before `c`. Module-name ordering is what the rest of the diff follows (`purchase_verdicts.py` and `purchase_accounting.py` both list `cutover_*` before `manta_trading`), and the mandated ruff config includes the `I` rule, under which this block is unsorted. I could not inspect `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml` (excluded from the diff scope), so please confirm `ruff check` passes on this file; if the `I` rule is active for `scripts/`, move the two `purchase_*` imports after `cutover_common`.

findings.title: --estimate exits 0 and prints the ceiling command even when the verdict is "refused" for a non-ceiling reason, without narrating the reason
findings.description: Description: With `check_ceilings=False`, `judge_estimate` (`scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:193-231`) returns `Estimate.BUY` for *any* non-`nothing_to_buy` verdict — including a `refused` verdict — and `_estimate_only` prints `verdict {verdict}: buy` plus the ceiling command, but never prints `summary["reasons"]` to the terminal (they only reach the narration file inside the raw JSON logged by `fetch_estimate`). The refused-for-a-short-ceiling case is the intended D4 flow, but I did not fully trace `spend_guard.evaluate_spend`'s estimate-only refusals (unverified): if a refusal can arise for a non-ceiling reason (e.g. a space verdict reason appended in `plan_summary`), the operator gets a command and exit 0 with the cause visible only in the log file. Printing `summary["reasons"]` in `_estimate_only` would close the gap cheaply.

findings.title: Resubmit-origin matching assumes reset re-stamps requested_at (unverified)
findings.description: Description: `resubmit_origins` matches a resubmit to the earliest *jobless* row of the same `(schema, range)` and `_check_resubmit` requires that row's `requested_at` to be ≥ the cutover start. I could not read the `reset` implementation (unverified): if `reset` puts a row back to `requested` while *preserving* the original `requested_at`, then a re-run of the same cutover after a failed pass + reset would judge its own resubmit as "before this cutover started" and stop, leaving the cutover unfinishable without manual intervention. The matching direction is otherwise sound (earliest-wins can only look older, never newer; the shared-range key intentionally omits product, per the docstring), and refusal is the safe direction — but the reset-timestamp behavior is worth confirming, since a false stop here blocks the whole slice rather than just flagging a finding.
